definition_en: to believe someone may be guilty, or a person thought to be guilty
core_image: 警探在灯下翻看档案，目光停在一个人名上
scene: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。The police suspect that he hid the money.
sceneCN: 这里 suspect 是「怀疑」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。

senses.definition: to think that someone may be guilty or dishonest

senses.example: The police suspect that he hid the money.
senses.exampleCN: 警方怀疑他把钱藏了起来。
senses.why: This is the core sense of suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 这是「怀疑」的核心义项。

senses.title: A person believed guilty
senses.definition: a person believed to have committed a crime

senses.example: The suspect was held for questioning.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑犯被拘留审问。
senses.why: As a noun the word names the person.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时指人。

senses.title: Likely to be bad or false
senses.definition: likely to be bad, false, or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 可能是坏的、假的或危险的
senses.example: They found a suspect package by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门边发现一个可疑包裹。
senses.why: As an adjective it describes things that raise doubt.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时描述引起怀疑的事物。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a feeling to a person to a thing.
abstract.cn: 这个词轻易地从感觉转到人，再转到物。

definition_en: to stop or delay something, or to hang something from above
core_image: 钟摆从上方垂下，停在半空中
scene: 比赛因大雨暂停了。The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 suspend 是「暂停」（第 1 个义项）；句意：比赛因大雨暂停了。

senses.title: To stop temporarily
senses.definition: to stop something for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 使某事停止一段时间
senses.example: The match was suspended because of heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛因大雨暂停了。
senses.why: This is the common sense of a temporary stop.
senses.whyCN: 这是「暂时停止」的常见义项。

senses.title: To hang from above
senses.definition: to hang something so that it is held from above
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从上吊起

senses.exampleCN: 一盏灯悬挂在天花板上。
senses.why: This is the original physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的物理义项。

senses.title: To remove someone temporarily
senses.definition: to make someone leave their job or school for a time
senses.definitionCN: 使某人暂时离开工作或学校

senses.exampleCN: 他被停学一周。
senses.why: Here the stopping applies to a person's position.
senses.whyCN: 这里停止的是人的职位。

definition_zh: 可持续的；可长期维持的；（不耗尽资源而）能长期继续的；长期可行的
definition_en: able to be continued over the long term without destroying or exhausting the resources or conditions it depends on
core_image: 一只渔篓只取走水面一层鱼，留下大部分鱼群继续繁殖，旁边的日历翻过一年又一年
scene: 这里指「可持续的」。 The project aims for sustainable growth rather than a short-term boom.
sceneCN: 这里 sustainable 是「可持续增长」（第 3 个义项：增长不以透支未来为代价）；句意：该项目追求可持续增长，而不是短期繁荣。图中可辨识物件：渔篓、鱼群、逐年翻过的日历、缓缓上升的曲线、没有断裂的阶梯。

pos.zh: 可持续的；可长期维持的；（环境）不耗尽资源的；长期可行的

derivatives.zh: 可持续性（sustainable + -ity「性质」，语义由形容词偏移为抽象名词）
维持；支撑（源自古法语 sustenir = 拉丁 sustinere「自下托住」）
食物；生计（sustain + -ance「……之物」，由「支撑」偏移为「维持生命之物」）

senses.title: Kind to the environment
senses.titleCN: 环境上可持续的：不破坏、不耗尽自然
senses.definition: describing an activity or product that can continue without destroying or exhausting the natural environment it depends on
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种能够持续进行、而不破坏或耗尽所依赖的自然环境的活动或产品
senses.example: The factory switched to sustainable energy sources.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂改用可持续的能源。
senses.why: This is the modern headline sense: the word promises that a practice will not consume its own base. The Latin picture of holding up from below becomes the environment holding up the activity.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最显眼的义项：该词承诺一种做法不会消耗自身根基。拉丁语「自下托住」的画面变成环境托住这项活动。

senses.title: A rate or level that can be kept up
senses.titleCN: 可长期维持的速率或水平
senses.definition: describing a speed, level or pace that can be continued over time without falling or collapsing
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种可以长期保持、不致下滑或崩溃的速度、水平或节奏
senses.example: The team set a sustainable pace for the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为漫长的攀登设定了一个可持续的节奏。
senses.why: Here the word is applied to quantities: a pace is sustainable if the body or the budget can repeat it. The test is whether the rate outlasts the effort.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词用于数量：只要身体或预算能重复执行，节奏就是可持续的。检验标准是速率能否比努力更长久。

senses.title: Growth that does not overheat
senses.titleCN: 可持续增长：不过热、不透支的增长
senses.definition: describing economic or organizational growth that can continue without overheating, crashing or consuming its own future
senses.definitionCN: 描述能够持续进行、而不致过热、崩溃或消耗自身未来的经济或组织增长
senses.example: Analysts welcomed the shift toward sustainable growth.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师欢迎向可持续增长的转变。
senses.why: Economists use the word for expansion that stays within real limits of credit, labor and demand. A boom is fast; sustainable growth is fast enough to last.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用该词指停留在信贷、劳动力与需求真实限度内的扩张。繁荣是快的；可持续增长则是快得能持久。

senses.title: Farming that protects the soil
senses.titleCN: 可持续农业：保护土壤与水源的耕作
senses.definition: describing agricultural methods that preserve soil, water and biodiversity while producing food over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 描述在长期产粮的同时保住土壤、水源与生物多样性的农业方法
senses.example: Sustainable agriculture rotates crops to protect the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续农业通过轮作来保护土壤。
senses.why: In farming the word measures the ground itself: a method is sustainable if the field still produces in fifty years. The image of holding up from below becomes literal topsoil.
senses.whyCN: 在农业中，该词以土地本身为尺度：一片田地五十年后仍能产出，方法才算可持续。「自下托住」的意象变成了字面上的表土。

senses.title: Materials and buildings with a light footprint
senses.titleCN: 可持续材料与建筑：低环境代价的建造
senses.definition: describing materials, products or buildings that can be produced, used and maintained with low environmental cost over their life cycle
senses.definitionCN: 描述在整个生命周期内能以较低环境代价被生产、使用与维护的材料、产品或建筑
senses.example: The architects chose sustainable timber for the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师为框架选择了可持续木材。
senses.why: In construction and design the adjective certifies a whole life cycle, from harvest to disposal. It is the environmental sense applied to things rather than activities.
senses.whyCN: 在建筑与设计中，该形容词为从采伐到废弃的整个生命周期作担保。这是环境义项从活动延伸到物品。

senses.title: A business model that survives
senses.definition: describing a business model or income source that can continue earning enough to operate over the long term
senses.definitionCN: 描述能够长期持续赚到足够运营收入的商业模式或收入来源
senses.example: A subscription model proved more sustainable than one-off sales.
senses.exampleCN: 订阅模式被证明比一次性销售更可持续。
senses.why: In business English the word is about survival without constant rescue: revenue must cover costs year after year. The system keeps itself going.
senses.whyCN: 在商业英语中，该词指无需不断救援而能生存：收入必须年复一年地覆盖成本。系统自己维持自己。

senses.title: A lifestyle a person can maintain
senses.definition: describing a habit, diet or way of living that a person can continue without burning out or giving up
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个人能够长期坚持、不致耗尽精力或放弃的习惯、饮食或生活方式
senses.example: The diet is sustainable because it allows occasional treats.
senses.exampleCN: 这种饮食法允许偶尔犒劳自己，所以能够坚持。
senses.why: Health and productivity writers apply the word to willpower: a plan is sustainable if the person can repeat it next month. The scale is one life, not the planet.
senses.whyCN: 健康与效率类作者把该词用在意志力上：一个人下个月还能照做的计划才是可持续的。尺度是一个人的生活，而不是整个地球。

senses.title: A harvest that does not deplete the stock
senses.titleCN: 可持续产量：不耗尽资源的采收
senses.definition: describing a harvest, catch or extraction level that removes no more than the resource can replace
senses.definitionCN: 描述移除量不超过资源再生量的采收、捕捞或开采水平
senses.example: The quota was set at a sustainable yield.
senses.exampleCN: 配额被定在可持续产量的水平上。
senses.why: Fisheries and forestry use the word for the maximum that can be taken forever: take the interest, keep the capital. It is the oldest precise sense of the modern environmental meaning.
senses.whyCN: 渔业与林业用该词指可永远采走的最大量：只取利息，保住本金。这是现代环境义项中最古老而精确的用法。

intro.en: Sustainable is sustain plus the adjective ending -able; sustain came through Old French sustenir from Latin sustinere, made of sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: sustainable 是 sustain 加形容词词尾 -able；sustain 经古法语 sustenir 源自拉丁 sustinere，由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」组成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sustinere 'to hold up from below, support, endure' was built on sub- 'from below' and tenere 'to hold, keep'. It already covered both physical support and enduring hardship.
items.cn: 拉丁 sustinere「自下托住、支撑、承受」由 sub-「自下」与 tenere「握住、保持」构成；它既有物理支撑义，也有忍受苦难义。

items.en: English took sustain through Old French sustenir in the medieval period, with the meanings 'to keep in being, maintain, provide for'.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪经古法语 sustenir 借入 sustain，义为「使存续、维持、供养」。

items.en: Sustainable was formed on sustain with -able; in the seventeenth century it meant 'able to be supported or maintained', used of arguments, weights and provisions. Its first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: sustainable 由 sustain 加 -able 构成；十七世纪时义为「可被支撑或维持的」，用于论证、重物与给养。其最早书证年代存疑。

items.en: The environmental sense arose in the 1970s and 1980s, and the phrase sustainable development became a global policy term after the 1987 Brundtland report.
items.cn: 环境义项在二十世纪七八十年代兴起；sustainable development 一词在 1987 年《布伦特兰报告》后成为全球政策用语。

items.en: Economics and engineering fixed the modern range of the adjective: sustainable growth, sustainable yield, sustainable energy, sustainable materials.
items.cn: 经济学与工程学固定了该形容词的现代义域：可持续增长、可持续产量、可持续能源、可持续材料。

items.en: The exact first English citation of sustainable is uncertain. The deeper root of tenere is generally taken to be reconstructed Indo-European *ten- 'to stretch, hold', a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sustainable 的英语最早书证年代不确定。tenere 的更深词根一般认为是重构的印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」，属重构形式，而非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the sustain family by part of speech; the second contrasts sustainable with near-synonyms, since sustainable stresses not exhausting resources and lasting over the long term.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 sustain 词族；第二组将 sustainable 与近义词对照，因为 sustainable 强调不耗尽资源、可长期维持。

entries.definition: Continuous over a period. Sustained describes effort that went on; sustainable asks whether it can go on without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续的；sustained 描述确实持续下去的努力，sustainable 追问它能否无损害地继续。

entries.definition: The verb of keeping something going. Sustainable is the adjective formed on it with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指维持某物；sustainable 是它加 -able 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The concrete means of staying alive. Sustainable describes the quality of a practice, not the food itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指维持生命的具体手段；sustainable 描述做法的性质，而非食物本身。

entries.definition: The abstract noun. Sustainable is the quality; sustainability is the name of the quality and of the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 抽象名词；sustainable 是性质，sustainability 是这一性质及其运动的名称。

entries.definition: Able to be kept in working order. Maintained implies constant input and care; sustainable implies the system can go on without exhausting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指可保持良好运转；maintained 隐含需要不断投入与维护，sustainable 隐含系统能不耗尽自身而继续。

entries.definition: Able to work or succeed. Viable is about feasibility now; sustainable adds the demand that it last without damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指能行得通、能成功；viable 关乎眼下可行，sustainable 还要求无损害地长久延续。

entries.definition: Able to be replenished by natural processes. Renewable describes the source; sustainable describes the whole practice that respects the source.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被自然过程补充；renewable 描述资源本身，sustainable 描述尊重该资源的整个做法。

entries.definition: Resistant to wear. Durable is about physical toughness; sustainable is about not consuming what keeps the system alive.
entries.definitionCN: 指耐磨、结实；durable 关乎物理强度，sustainable 关乎不消耗维持系统存活的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sustain + -able: able to be held up, hence able to keep going.
normal.cn: sustain + -able：托得住，因而撑得久。

normal.en: The family runs sustain, sustainable, sustainability, sustained, sustenance, unsustainable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sustain、sustainable、sustainability、sustained、sustenance、unsustainable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases fix the range: sustainable development, sustainable growth, sustainable yield, sustainable energy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标定义域：可持续发展、可持续增长、可持续产量、可持续能源。

normal.en: Sustainable fishing takes no more than what regrows.
normal.cn: 可持续捕捞只取再生长的那部分。

normal.en: A sustainable pace is one you can repeat tomorrow.
normal.cn: 可持续的节奏是明天还能照做的节奏。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that yields fruit every year because the picker never strips it bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵每年都结果的树，因为采摘者从不把它摘光。

abstract.en: Picture a runner keeping a pace slow enough to finish the whole race.
abstract.cn: 想象一位跑者把节奏放慢到足以跑完全程。

abstract.en: Picture a well that stays full because no one pumps more than the rain returns.
abstract.cn: 想象一口总也不见底的井，因为没人抽得比雨水回补更多。

examples.en: The farm switched to sustainable practices that protect the topsoil.
examples.cn: 这家农场改用保护表土的可持续做法。

examples.en: Analysts doubted the project was financially sustainable without subsidies.
examples.cn: 分析师怀疑没有补贴，这个项目在财务上是否可持续。

examples.en: A sustainable workload keeps the whole team healthy year-round.
examples.cn: 可持续的工作量让整个团队全年保持健康。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 「sustain（维持）+ able（可……的）」——撑得住、耗不尽 → sustainable 可持续的

root: 拉丁 sustinere = sub-「自下」+ tenere「握住、保持」→ 古法语 sustenir → 英语 sustain + -able「可……的」。更深词根一般认为是印欧语 *ten-「伸展、保持」（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one test — can it keep going? — applied to nature, rates, growth, farming, materials, business, habits and harvests.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用同一道考题——能否一直运转？——分别施于自然、速率、增长、农业、材料、商业、习惯与收成。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is held up from below so it can keep going without breaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被从下方托住，得以持续运转而不垮。

branches.en: NATURAL RESOURCES: energy, farming and harvests do not deplete the base they draw on.
branches.cn: 自然资源：能源、农业与收成不耗尽其所依托的根基。

branches.en: RATES AND GROWTH: paces, levels and expansions can be kept up without collapse.
branches.cn: 速率与增长：节奏、水平与扩张可持续而不崩溃。

branches.en: MATERIALS AND BUILDINGS: products and structures are made and maintained at low environmental cost.
branches.cn: 材料与建筑：产品与结构以低环境代价制造与维护。

branches.en: BUSINESS SURVIVAL: a model earns enough to keep operating over the long term.
branches.cn: 商业生存：模式长期能赚到足以运营的收入。

branches.en: PERSONAL HABITS: a practice can be repeated without burning out.
branches.cn: 个人习惯：做法可反复执行而不致枯竭。

intro.en: Sustainable is sustain plus the adjective suffix -able: the Latin verb sustinere 'hold up from below' and the ending that says 'able to be'.
intro.cn: sustainable 是 sustain 加形容词词尾 -able：即拉丁动词 sustinere「自下托住」加「可……」的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is tenere 'to hold, keep' with sub- 'from below'; -able reached English through French from Latin -abilis. The same family includes tenable, retain and maintain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 tenere「握住、保持」加 sub-「自下」；-able 经法语源自拉丁 -abilis。同一词族还有 tenable、retain、maintain。

items.meaning: able to be continued without exhausting the base
items.meaningCN: 可持续的；不耗尽根基而能继续的
items.example: They chose sustainable materials for the floors.
items.exampleCN: 他们为地板选择了可持续材料。

items.meaning: to hold up, keep in being
items.example: The region cannot sustain its growing population.
items.exampleCN: 该地区无法养活不断增长的人口。

items.example: Sustainability shaped the company's product line.
items.exampleCN: 可持续性影响了公司的产品线。

items.example: The team showed sustained effort all season.
items.exampleCN: 全队整个赛季都表现出持续的努力。

items.example: The refugees found sustenance in the mountain villages.
items.exampleCN: 难民在山村找到了食物与生计。
这场繁荣被证明不可持续。

items.meaning: able to be held or defended
items.example: The theory is tenable only with new evidence.
items.exampleCN: 只有在新的证据下，这个理论才站得住脚。

items.structure: Latin manu tenere (to hold in hand) via Old French

definition_zh: 沼泽；湿地；淹没（土地）；使（船）灌水；使应接不暇
definition_en: an area of low, wet ground where water collects and trees or tall plants grow; to flood land or fill a boat with water; to overwhelm someone with too much of something
core_image: 一片低洼地常年积水，柳树干和芦苇把根泡在浑黄的静水里
scene: 连日暴雨后，河水漫过低地，柳树和芦苇都泡在齐膝深的浑水里。After days of rain the river spread over the low field and turned it into a swamp.
sceneCN: 这里 swamp 指「长着树木或高草的积水低地」（第 1 个义项：以木本植物为主的湿地）；句意：连日降雨后河水漫过低地，把它变成了一片沼泽。图中可辨识物件：齐膝的浑水、柳树干、芦苇丛、漫过田埂的河面。

pos.zh: 沼泽；湿地（木本或草本植物茂盛的积水低地）
淹没（土地）；使（船）灌满水；使应接不暇、被大量事物压垮

collocations.zh: 以大量低价商品冲击市场

senses.title: Forested wetland with standing water
senses.titleCN: 长着树木的积水低地（木本沼泽）
senses.definition: a low area of land where water stands for much of the year and trees such as willows or cypresses grow in it
senses.definitionCN: 常年积水的低洼地，柳树、落羽杉等树木生长其中
senses.example: After days of rain the river spread over the low field and turned it into a swamp.
senses.exampleCN: 连日降雨后，河水漫过低地，把它变成了一片沼泽。
senses.why: the noun names the ground itself, and the defining features are low position, standing water and rooted plants that tolerate wet soil.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指地面本身，其要点是地势低、常年积水、并且长着耐湿的扎根植物。

senses.title: Any marshy or boggy ground
senses.definition: broadly, any soft wet ground that gives way underfoot, whether or not trees grow on it
senses.definitionCN: 泛指任何踩上去会下陷的湿软地面，无论其上是否长树
senses.example: The path crossed a reed swamp before it reached the dunes.
senses.exampleCN: 小路穿过一片芦苇荡，才到达沙丘。
senses.why: the tree sense is the prototype, but speakers extend the word to reedy and grassy wetlands because the shared feature is saturated ground, not woodiness.
senses.whyCN: 树木只是原型特征；说话人把它扩展到芦苇沼泽与草甸，因为共同点是土壤饱和，而非有树。

senses.title: Flood dry land
senses.definition: to cover an area of land with water so that it becomes marshy or impassable
senses.definitionCN: 用水覆盖一片土地，使其变成沼泽或无法通行
senses.example: The burst canal swamped the lower pastures within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 运河决口后一小时内就淹没了下游的牧场。
senses.why: the verb reverses the noun's usual state: land that was dry is made into the thing the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的状态倒转过来：原本干燥的土地被造成名词所指的那种地方。

senses.title: Fill a boat with water
senses.definition: to fill a small boat with water so that it sinks or is in danger of sinking
senses.definitionCN: 使小船灌满水而下沉或濒临下沉
senses.example: A following sea swamped the dinghy just beyond the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 一道尾随浪在礁石外把小艇灌满了水。
senses.why: a boat swamped by water is in the same condition as land swamped by a flood, so the same verb serves both objects.
senses.whyCN: 被水灌满的船与被洪水淹没的地处在同一种状态，因此同一个动词可以带两类宾语。

senses.title: Overwhelm with too much work
senses.titleCN: 被大量工作或事务压得应接不暇
senses.definition: to give someone far more work, requests or information than they can handle
senses.definitionCN: 给某人的工作、请求或信息远超其所能处理的数量
senses.example: The small office was swamped with applications in the final week.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周，这家小办公室被申请材料淹没了。
senses.why: the metaphor is water over land: an amount that rises above capacity is felt as flooding, so the object is buried rather than merely busy.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻来自水淹陆地：超出承受量的东西像水上涨，人被埋在其中，而不只是忙碌。

senses.title: Defeat by sheer numbers
senses.titleCN: 以数量压倒、使无法招架
senses.definition: to defeat or outnumber an opponent so heavily that resistance collapses
senses.definitionCN: 以绝对数量击败或压过对手，使其抵抗崩溃
senses.example: Cheap imports swamped the local makers within two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口货在两个销售季内就压垮了本地制造商。
senses.why: from flooding the physical sense passes to competition: a market or an army is 'drowned' by numbers it cannot match.
senses.whyCN: 从淹没实物的用法过渡到竞争：市场或军队被无法匹敌的数量「淹掉」。

senses.title: A situation that traps and slows you
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：使人陷住、难以脱身的困境
senses.definition: a difficult situation that absorbs time and energy and prevents progress, as mud holds a walker
senses.definitionCN: 耗费时间精力、使人无法前进的困难处境，如泥沼拖住行人
senses.example: The project sank into a swamp of approvals and revisions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目陷进了审批与改稿的泥沼。
senses.why: wet ground that pulls at the feet is a natural image for bureaucracy or debt, so the noun is used for any sticky predicament.
senses.whyCN: 会拽住双脚的湿地是官僚程序或债务的天然意象，因此名词可指任何黏住人的困境。

senses.title: Flood a market with goods
senses.titleCN: 以大量商品涌入并冲击市场
senses.definition: to supply a market with so much of a product that prices or rivals are forced down
senses.definitionCN: 向市场投入过多某种产品，压低价位或挤垮对手
senses.example: Two firms swamped the market with low-cost panels that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那年冬天，两家公司用低价板材淹没了市场。
senses.why: this is sense 3 applied to commerce: the market is the land, goods are the water, and excess is the flood.
senses.whyCN: 这是第 3 个义项在商业上的投射：市场是陆地，商品是水，过量就是洪水。

intro.en: Swamp is a Middle English noun for wet low ground, first recorded around 1500. Its deeper origin is not settled: a Middle Dutch or Middle Low German source has been proposed, and a link with the Germanic word for 'sponge' is plausible but unproven.
intro.cn: swamp 是中古英语指湿低地的名词，约 1500 年首次见于记载。其更深来源尚无定论：有人提出它来自中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，也有人把它与日耳曼语中「海绵」一词联系起来，但均未得到证实。

items.en: Swampe is recorded around 1500 with the sense 'watery land, marsh', the earliest use of the word in English.
items.cn: swampe 约在 1500 年以「积水地、沼泽」义进入记载，这是该词在英语中最早的用法。

items.en: A Middle Dutch or Middle Low German swamp 'marsh, sponge' is often suggested as the source; the geographic spread of the form makes a borrowing likely but not demonstrated.
items.cn: 常有人认为来源是中古荷兰语或中古低地德语的 swamp「沼泽、海绵」；该词形的地理分布使借入说较可信，但尚未被证明。

items.en: The comparison with the Germanic word for sponge rests on the idea of ground that soaks up water; this is a semantic hypothesis, not a proven cognate relation.
items.cn: 与日耳曼语「海绵」词的比较建立在「会吸水的土地」这一想法上；这只是语义假说，并非已证实的同源关系。

items.en: By the seventeenth century swamp was used as a verb meaning 'to submerge or flood', and the nautical sense 'to fill a boat with water' grew from it.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，swamp 已用作动词，意为「淹没、灌水」，航海义「使船灌满水」由此产生。

items.en: The figurative use 'to overwhelm with numbers or quantity' appears later and is now the most frequent meaning in news and business writing.
items.cn: 「以数量压倒」的比喻义出现较晚，如今已成为新闻与商业写作中最常见的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic form is reconstructed, and no single ancestor can be named with confidence.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：其日耳曼语之前的形式属重构，无法有把握地指认单一祖形。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble swamp in spelling or sound but are unrelated; group two holds wetland and flooding words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 swamp 拼写或读音相近但并无词源关系的词；第二组是共享部分词义的湿地与淹没类词。

entries.definition: A mass of insects or people moving together; it differs from swamp by one letter and has its own Germanic origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指成群移动的昆虫或人；与 swamp 只差一个字母，但另有日耳曼语来源。

entries.definition: To bring the foot down hard, or a printed mark; the shared -amp ending is accidental, not etymological.
entries.definitionCN: 指用力跺脚，或印出的标记；共同的 -amp 词尾只是巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: To trade one thing for another; it sounds close to swamp but comes from a separate Germanic root.
entries.definitionCN: 指以物易物；读音接近 swamp，但来自另一条日耳曼语词根。

entries.definition: To strike a small insect with something flat; the similarity is only phonetic.
entries.definitionCN: 指用扁平物拍打小虫；相似之处仅在读音。

entries.definition: Low wet ground usually covered with grass and reeds rather than trees; swamp often implies woody growth.
entries.definitionCN: 通常长草与芦苇而非树木的低湿地面；swamp 往往暗示有木本植物。

entries.definition: Wet ground built of partly decayed plant matter, soft enough to swallow a walker; it stresses peat, swamp stresses standing water.
entries.definitionCN: 由半腐植物堆积成的湿地，软到能吞住行人；它强调泥炭，swamp 强调积水。

entries.definition: The scientific umbrella term for all saturated land, including swamps, marshes and bogs; it is neutral and policy-oriented.
entries.definitionCN: 对所有饱和土地的科学统称，包括沼泽、草沼与泥炭地；语气中立，多用于政策文本。

entries.definition: To cover land with a flood, or to overwhelm with a quantity; it is the formal Latin-based counterpart of the verb swamp.
entries.definitionCN: 指洪水淹没土地，或以大量事物压倒；是动词 swamp 的拉丁语系正式对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds and real collocations of the word, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The everyday phrase 'be swamped with work' carries the flooding metaphor: work rises like water over the desk.
normal.cn: 常用短语 be swamped with work 带着洪水的隐喻：工作像水一样涨过桌面。

normal.en: Wetland types line up as swamp, marsh, bog and fen, each with a different dominant plant and water chemistry.
normal.cn: 湿地类型可以排成 swamp、marsh、bog、fen，各自优势植物与水质不同。

normal.en: The adjective swampy is the regular -y derivative, as in 'swampy ground' and 'a swampy smell'.
normal.cn: 形容词 swampy 是规则的 -y 派生，如「泥泞的地面」「沼泽的气味」。

normal.en: 'Drain the swamp' is a fixed political idiom for removing entrenched corruption.
normal.cn: drain the swamp 是固定的政治习语，指清除盘根错节的腐败。

normal.en: Nautical use survives in 'the boat was swamped by a wave', where water fills the hull.
normal.cn: 航海用法仍见于 「the boat was swamped by a wave」，指浪把水灌进船体。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where papers rise like floodwater until only the top of the lamp shows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，文件像洪水上涨，最后只剩台灯顶部露出水面。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall buried under identical cheap goods until no other seller can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位被一模一样的便宜货埋住，别的卖家都看不见了。

abstract.en: Picture boots pulled deeper with every step, so progress costs more than it returns.
abstract.cn: 想象每走一步靴子就陷得更深，前进的代价大于收获。

examples.en: The cypress swamp stays under water for most of the year.
examples.cn: 这片落羽杉沼泽一年中大部分时间都泡在水里。

examples.en: The office was swamped with complaints after the new timetable began.
examples.cn: 新时刻表启用后，办公室被投诉淹没了。

examples.en: One heavy wave swamped the dinghy before the crew could bail.
examples.cn: 船员还没来得及舀水，一个大浪就把小艇灌满了。

dict_mnemonic.note: 谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 「swamp」读似「水漫坡」——水漫上低坡，坡地就成了沼泽；工作堆成水，人也被淹没

root: 中古英语 swampe「积水低地」（约 1500 年），更深来源不确定；常被联系到中古荷兰语或中古低地德语 swamp「沼泽、海绵」，仅为假说，未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: water standing where it should not. The noun names the ground, the verb floods land or fills a hull, and from that flooding come the senses of being overwhelmed, outnumbered, trapped and swamped in a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：水停在它本不该停的地方。名词指那片地面，动词指淹没土地或灌满船体，再由「淹没」引申出被压垮、被数量压倒、被困住以及冲击市场等义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: low ground where water stands among rooted plants.
core.cn: 核心意象：低洼地里，水停在扎根植物之间。

branches.en: WETLAND TYPES: the noun splits by dominant plants, from trees to reeds.
branches.cn: 湿地类型：名词按优势植物分为有树与有苇两类。

branches.en: LAND FLOODED: dry ground is made into the noun's own condition.
branches.cn: 淹地：干燥地面被造成名词所指的状态。

branches.en: HULL FILLED: a boat takes on water as land does in a flood.
branches.cn: 灌船：船进水，与洪水中的陆地同理。

branches.en: OVERWHELMED: quantity or difficulty rises above capacity and pins the person down.
branches.cn: 被压垮：数量或难度超过承受力，把人困住。

branches.en: MARKET FLOODED: goods behave like floodwater and force prices down.
branches.cn: 市场被淹：商品像洪水，压低了价格。

intro.en: Swamp is a native Germanic noun with no productive prefix; its family is built by the adjective suffix -y, the noun-forming -ness, and noun compounds such as swampland and swamp gas.
intro.cn: swamp 是日耳曼语本族名词，没有能产的前缀；其词族由形容词后缀 -y、名词后缀 -ness 以及 swampland、swamp gas 这类复合名词构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for swamp. Latin palus 'marsh' and stagnum 'pool' translate the idea but are semantic equivalents, not cognates, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: swamp 没有拉丁语来源。拉丁 palus「沼泽」与 stagnum「水塘」只是语义对应词，并非同源词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaning: wet ground; to flood or overwhelm
items.example: The swamp lies below the ridge.

items.meaning: like a swamp; soft and waterlogged
items.example: The trail turned swampy after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨后小路变得泥泞积水。

items.example: Much of the swampland was drained for farms.
items.exampleCN: 大片沼泽地被排干改为农田。

items.example: The swampiness of the field delayed the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 田里的泥泞积水延误了收割。

items.meaning: methane rising from decaying wetland plants
items.example: Swamp gas flickered over the marsh at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 黄昏时沼泽沼气在草沼上方闪动。

items.example: A swamp cooler kept the dry room bearable.
items.exampleCN: 一台蒸发式冷风机让干燥的房间勉强可待。

items.meaning: woodland rooted in permanent standing water
items.example: The swamp forest floods every spring.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽林每年春天被水淹没。

items.meaning: a North American oak of wet soils
items.meaningCN: 沼生白栎（北美湿生栎树）
items.example: Swamp white oak tolerates seasonal flooding.
items.exampleCN: 沼生白栎能耐季节性水淹。

definition_zh: 交换；互换；用…替换；把…换掉
definition_en: to give something to someone and receive something in return, or to replace one thing with another
core_image: 两只手同时递出和接回：东西在掌心之间换了个位置
scene: 午休时，小丽不想吃自己盒饭里的鸡腿，隔壁的同学正好爱吃鸡腿。They agreed to swap the chicken leg for a piece of chocolate cake.
sceneCN: 这里 swap 是「交换、互换」（第 1 个义项：拿一样东西换另一样东西）；句意是他们商量好用鸡腿换一块巧克力蛋糕。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示动作者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「交换者」，使用频率较低
复合名词，义为「旧货交换集市」，主要见于美式英语

senses.title: To exchange one thing for another
senses.definition: to give one thing to someone and receive a different thing in return
senses.definitionCN: 把一样东西给别人，同时换回另一样东西
senses.example: The kids swapped baseball cards during recess.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在课间交换棒球卡。
senses.why: The core image of two hands passing things in opposite directions naturally gives the basic meaning of exchanging items.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两只手朝相反方向递东西，最自然地长出「拿物换物」这一基本义。

senses.title: To replace one thing with another
senses.definition: to take one thing out of a place or role and put a different thing there instead
senses.definitionCN: 把一样东西从某个位置或用途中拿走，换成另一样
senses.example: You should swap the flat tire for the spare one.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该把爆胎换上备用胎。
senses.why: Once two things trade positions, the thing left behind has been replaced, extending the sense from mutual exchange to substitution.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西换了位置之后，原来的东西就被换下来了，词义由「互换取物」延伸为「替换」。

senses.title: To exchange information or words
senses.definition: to share news, ideas, or remarks with someone in a back-and-forth way
senses.definitionCN: 以一来一往的方式与某人分享消息、想法或说话
senses.example: The two scientists swapped opinions for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 两位科学家交流观点聊了几个小时。
senses.why: Conversation is itself an exchange: words travel back and forth like the objects in the core image.
senses.whyCN: 交谈本身就是一种往来，话语像核心意象中的物件一样来回传递，于是长出「交流、交谈」的抽象义。

senses.title: To trade shifts, roles, or duties
senses.definition: to agree with someone that each of you will do the other's shift, role, or task
senses.definitionCN: 与对方约定各自接替对方的班次、角色或任务
senses.example: Can I swap shifts with you next Friday?
senses.exampleCN: 下周五我能和你换个班吗？
senses.why: A duty can be handed over just like a physical object, so the exchange image applies to jobs and roles.
senses.whyCN: 职责可以像实物一样被交到另一个人手里，交换的意象便套用在班次与角色上。

senses.title: An act of exchanging things
senses.definition: an occasion when two people or groups exchange things
senses.definitionCN: 双方互相交换东西的一次行为或场合
senses.example: The deal was a swap of oil for grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易是用石油换粮食。
senses.why: A repeated action becomes a noun: the whole event of two hands passing things gets named.
senses.whyCN: 动作反复发生便被命名，两手互递东西的整个事件凝固为名词「一次交换」。

senses.title: A thing that has been exchanged
senses.definition: the item received in an exchange, especially in children's games or collections
senses.definitionCN: 在交换中拿到的东西，多见于儿童游戏或收藏活动
senses.example: She showed me her swaps from the sticker fair.
senses.exampleCN: 她给我看她从贴纸集市换来的宝贝。
senses.why: The result of the exchange, not the act itself, becomes the thing talked about, a regular noun shift.
senses.whyCN: 被谈论的对象从「交换这件事」转到「换回来的结果」，是名词义从动作到结果的常规转移。

senses.title: To change one choice or plan for another
senses.definition: to decide to use or do something different from what was first planned or chosen
senses.definitionCN: 决定改用或改做与最初计划、选择不同的事
senses.example: We swapped the indoor picnic for a restaurant dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们放弃了室内野餐，改成去餐厅吃饭。
senses.why: Plans sit in the mind like objects in a hand; changing a plan is mentally putting one down and picking up another.
senses.whyCN: 计划像握在手中的东西，改换计划就是把一个放下、把另一个拿起，意象从实物移到抽象决定。

senses.title: To exchange currencies or financial instruments
senses.definition: in finance, to exchange one stream of payments, currency, or interest rates for another under an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在金融领域，按协议把一种现金流、货币或利率换成另一种
senses.example: The two banks signed a currency swap agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两家银行签署了货币互换协议。
senses.why: Finance borrows the everyday exchange image and fixes it as a technical term for exchanging streams of money.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了日常交换的画面，把「互换来去」固定为交换资金流的术语。

senses.title: To swap over or swap round
senses.definition: to make two things trade places so that each occupies the other's former position
senses.definitionCN: 让两样东西互换位置，各自占据对方原来的地方
senses.example: The teacher swapped the two desks round to make more space.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把两张课桌对调位置，好腾出更多空间。
senses.why: The phrase emphasizes the result of the exchange: the two items have literally traded positions.
senses.whyCN: 短语强调交换的结果：两样东西确实互换了位置，是「交换」义向空间格局的落实。

intro.en: Swap is a native English word whose earlier history is uncertain; it belongs to a small family of verbs describing hitting or moving back and forth, and its modern sense of exchanging appears to have developed from the idea of two things striking or crossing.
intro.cn: swap 是英语本土词，更早的来历不确定；它属于一小族描写击打或来回摆动的动词，现代「交换」义一般认为是由「两物相击、来去交错」的画面发展而来。

items.en: The verb swappen appears, meaning to strike or to move with a swinging or sweeping motion.
items.cn: 中世纪英语出现动词 swappen，意为击打，或以摆动、挥动的方式移动。

items.en: The extended senses 'to dash' and 'to strike down' are recorded; the word also begins to describe back-and-forth motion.
items.cn: 十六世纪记录了「猛冲、击倒」等引申义；这个词也开始描写一来一往的动作。

items.en: The exchange sense develops, first in informal use; some older dictionaries long treated it as slang, a sign of its colloquial origin.
items.cn: 「交换」义发展出来，最初见于口语；旧词典长期把它标为俚语，可见其口头来源。

items.en: The noun use (an act of exchange) becomes established, and the word spreads from speech into general written use.
items.cn: 名词用法（一次交换）确立下来，这个词从口语进入一般书面语。

items.en: Swap extends to information, duties, plans, and finance (currency swaps, interest rate swaps), while older strike senses survive only in dialects.
items.cn: swap 延伸到信息、班次、计划和金融领域（货币互换、利率掉期）；旧的「击打」义只残留在方言里。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain. Swap may be imitative of a swishing or striking sound; a link to the verb swerve or to low German words of similar meaning is sometimes suggested but not proven.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定。一般认为 swap 可能是模拟挥击声的拟声词；有学者把它与 swerve 或低地德语中意义相近的词相联系，但均无确证。

note.en: Words that look or sound like swap, and words that live nearby in the field of exchanging.
note.cn: 与 swap 拼写或发音相近的词，以及与「交换」义场相邻的词。

entries.definition: an area of soft, wet land; to flood or overwhelm
entries.definitionCN: 沼泽；淹没，使应接不暇。只是比 swap 多一个字母 p，词义完全不同，属拼写相近但词源无关

entries.definition: to hit sharply, especially an insect
entries.definitionCN: 猛击、拍打（尤指拍苍蝇）。与 swap 拼写相近；有趣的是 swap 的旧义正是「击打」，但现代两词应分开理解

entries.definition: to move slowly from side to side; to influence someone
entries.definitionCN: 摇摆；动摇，左右某人。发音与拼写都接近 swap，词源上一般不认为同源

entries.definition: to give and receive things in return; the act of doing so
entries.definitionCN: 交换；兑换。较正式，涵盖 swap 的核心义，常用于货币、书信、礼品等场景

entries.definition: to buy, sell, or exchange goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 交易；做买卖；对换。强调买卖或职业性往来，swap 更口语、更侧重一来一往的对换

entries.definition: to exchange goods without using money
entries.definitionCN: 以物易物、实物交换。特指不动用货币的交换，语域比 swap 更正式、更古老

entries.definition: to exchange things or ideas with each other
entries.definitionCN: 互换、互相交流。强调双方对等地来去，多见于书面语和固定搭配

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks that tie swap to its spelling, sound, and real-life uses.
normalIntro.cn: 五条接地气的联想，把 swap 和它的拼写、读音与生活用法绑在一起。

normal.en: swap sounds like 'swuap' — think of hands crossing in the air as two people hand things over at the same moment.
normal.cn: swap 读起来像「斯握铺」——想象两个人同时递东西，两只手在空中交叉而过。

normal.en: SW-A-P: Students Will Always Pass things around — that passing is swapping.
normal.cn: S-W-A-P 可记为「Students Will Always Pass」——学生总在传东西，传着传着就是交换。

normal.en: swap and swamp differ by one letter: you swap cards, but you get swamped with homework.
normal.cn: swap 与 swamp 只差一个字母：换卡片用 swap，作业多到「被淹」（应接不暇）用 swamp。

normal.en: In finance you will meet currency swap — banks literally handing money streams back and forth.
normal.cn: 金融里会遇到 currency swap（货币互换）——银行把两股资金流你来我往地递来递去。

normal.en: swap meet is a market where everything is obtained by swapping, not buying.

definition_en: to make a serious promise, or to use rude words

definition_en: a long-term living together of two different organisms, often with benefit to both
core_image: 珊瑚与体内的藻类并列，彼此交换养分，箭头双向流动
scene: 这里指「共生」。 The symbiosis between the coral and its algae keeps both alive in poor water.
sceneCN: 这里 symbiosis 是「共生」（第 1 个义项：两种生物长期共同生活）；句意：珊瑚与其藻类的共生让两者在贫瘠的水中都能存活。图中可辨识物件：珊瑚、体内的藻类、双向的养分箭头。

senses.title: Living Together
senses.titleCN: 共生：两种生物长期共同生活
senses.definition: a close and long-term living together of two different organisms
senses.definitionCN: 两种不同生物密切而长期地共同生活
senses.example: Symbiosis can last for the whole life of both partners.
senses.exampleCN: 共生可以持续双方的一生。
senses.why: The word joins Greek syn- 'together' and bios 'life'. Its core is cohabitation, not benefit; benefit is a later refinement, which is why the term can cover several kinds of relationship.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由希腊 syn-「一起」与 bios「生命」构成；核心是共同居住，而不是获益；获益是后来的细化，因此该术语能涵盖多种关系。

senses.title: Mutual Benefit
senses.definition: a symbiotic relationship in which both partners benefit
senses.definitionCN: 双方都从中获益的共生关系
senses.example: The symbiosis between the fig and its pollinator benefits both.
senses.exampleCN: 无花果与其传粉者的共生使双方受益。
senses.why: In everyday biology symbiosis usually means mutualism: each side gives something the other needs. The word has narrowed from cohabitation to profitable cohabitation.
senses.whyCN: 在日常生物学中，symbiosis 通常指互利共生：每一方都给出对方需要的东西；这个词已从「共同居住」收窄为「有利可图地共同居住」。

senses.title: One-Sided Cohabitation
senses.titleCN: 偏利共生：一方获益、一方无碍
senses.definition: a loose use of symbiosis for a relationship in which one partner gains and the other is unaffected
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地用共生指一方获益、另一方不受影响的关系
senses.example: Some authors call the barnacle's ride a symbiosis, though only the barnacle gains.
senses.exampleCN: 有些作者把藤壶的搭车称为共生，虽然只有藤壶获益。
senses.why: Because the root sense is only 'living together', the term can be stretched to commensalism. Careful writers then add a qualifier, such as commensal symbiosis, to avoid implying mutual gain.
senses.whyCN: 由于词根义只是「共同生活」，该术语可以被扩展到偏利共生；严谨的作者会加限定语，如共栖共生，以免暗示双方获利。

senses.title: Parasitism as Cohabitation
senses.titleCN: 寄生性共生：广义共生中的寄生
senses.definition: the broad sense of symbiosis that includes parasitism, since the partners still live together
senses.definitionCN: 把寄生也纳入的广义共生，因为双方仍共同生活
senses.example: In the broad sense, symbiosis includes parasitism as one extreme.
senses.exampleCN: 在广义上，共生把寄生作为其中一个极端包含在内。
senses.why: If symbiosis means only cohabitation, a parasite and its host qualify. This broad definition is common in ecology textbooks, while medical writing usually keeps the narrower mutual-benefit sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果共生只指共同居住，寄生物与宿主也符合条件；这一广义定义在生态学教材中常见，而医学写作通常保留较窄的互利义。

senses.title: Social Symbiosis
senses.titleCN: 社会共生：群体之间的相互依存
senses.definition: a mutually dependent relationship between social groups or institutions
senses.definitionCN: 社会群体或机构之间相互依赖的关系
senses.example: The city describes the symbiosis between its universities and its industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市用「共生」来描述大学与产业之间的关系。
senses.why: The biological word was given a wider, non-biological sense by 1921. It keeps the picture of two parties living together and each supplying what the other lacks.
senses.whyCN: 这个生物学词在 1921 年之后被赋予更宽的非生物学含义；它保留了双方共同生活、彼此补足所缺的画面。

senses.title: Industrial Symbiosis
senses.titleCN: 产业共生：企业间交换废料与能源
senses.definition: a network in which firms use one another's waste, heat or by-products
senses.definitionCN: 企业互相利用对方的废物、热能或副产品的网络
senses.example: Industrial symbiosis turned one factory's waste heat into another's power.
senses.exampleCN: 产业共生把一家工厂的废热变成了另一家的动力。
senses.why: Here the partners are firms and the exchanged resource is matter or energy. The term is a deliberate ecological metaphor: what one organism excretes, another consumes.
senses.whyCN: 这里伙伴是企业，交换的资源是物质或能量；这个术语是有意使用的生态隐喻：一个生物排出的，正是另一个生物摄入的。

senses.title: Ecological Partnership
senses.titleCN: 生态伙伴关系：生态系统层面的互补
senses.definition: a partnership between species or processes that keeps an ecosystem functioning
senses.definitionCN: 维持生态系统运转的物种或过程之间的伙伴关系
senses.example: The symbiosis of grazers and grasses keeps the savanna open.
senses.exampleCN: 食草动物与草的共生让稀树草原保持开阔。
senses.why: The sense scales the relationship from two organisms to a whole system. It is still cohabitation, but the unit is now the ecosystem and the benefit is stability.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把关系从两个生物扩展到整个系统；它仍是共同生活，但单位变成了生态系统，收益变成了稳定性。

senses.title: Technology and Society
senses.titleCN: 技术与社会的共生：相互塑造
senses.definition: a mutually shaping relationship between a technology and the society that uses it
senses.definitionCN: 一项技术与其使用社会之间相互塑造的关系
senses.example: The book studies the symbiosis of mobile phones and urban life.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书研究手机与城市生活的共生。
senses.why: This is the furthest extension: neither side merely hosts the other, each changes the other. It keeps the core idea of living together while dropping the biological host.
senses.whyCN: 这是最远的引申：双方都不只是容纳对方，而是互相改变；它保留了共同生活的核心观念，却去掉了生物学宿主。

intro.en: Symbiosis was borrowed from Greek in 1876 as a biological term, after an earlier English sense of 'communal life'. Its meaning has oscillated between mere cohabitation and mutual benefit ever since.
intro.cn: symbiosis 于 1876 年作为生物学词从希腊语借入，而在此之前英语已有「共同生活」的旧义；此后它的含义便在「单纯同居」与「互利」之间摆动。

items.en: Greek symbiosis meant 'a living together', from symbioun 'to live together' and symbios 'one living together, partner, companion, husband or wife'. The root idea is shared life, not necessarily shared benefit.
items.cn: 希腊 symbiosis 意为「共同生活」，来自 symbioun「一起生活」与 symbios「共同生活者、伙伴、同伴、丈夫或妻子」；其词根观念是共享生活，不一定是共享利益。

items.en: Syn- 'together' is the assimilated form of the prefix before labials, and bios means 'life, course of life'. The same bios underlies biology and microbe.
items.cn: syn-「一起」是该前缀在唇音前发生同化的形式；bios 意为「生命、生命历程」。同一个 bios 也构成 biology 与 microbe。

items.en: An English sense 'communal or social life' is recorded in the 1620s, long before the biological use. It shows that the word's social application is not a modern metaphor but an old branch.
items.cn: 英语中「共同或社会生活」的义项记录于十七世纪二十年代，远早于生物学用法；这说明该词的社会用法不是现代隐喻，而是一条古老的支线。

items.en: The biological sense 'union for life of two different organisms based on mutual benefit' is recorded from 1876. The definition already included benefit, though later textbooks widened it again.
items.cn: 「两种不同生物基于互利而终身结合」的生物学义项记录于 1876 年；这个定义已经包含获益，尽管后来的教材又把它拓宽。

items.en: Symbiont, for either partner, is recorded from 1887, earlier in German. Symbiotic is recorded from 1882, formed with -ic; its use for human activities dates from 1951.
items.cn: 指任一方的 symbiont 记录于 1887 年，德语中更早；symbiotic 记录于 1882 年，由 -ic 构成，其用于人类活动则始于 1951 年。

items.en: Ecology now places mutualism, commensalism and parasitism on a spectrum, sometimes calling all three symbiosis. The word's breadth is inherited from its Greek root, not invented by recent authors.
items.cn: 现代生态学把互利、偏利与寄生放在一个谱系上，有时把三者都称为共生；这个词的宽泛性承自希腊词根，而不是近代作者发明的。

note.en: The first group separates the relationship noun from its participants and adjective. The second group holds the three ecological relations that sit on the same spectrum.
note.cn: 第一组区分关系名词与参与方、形容词；第二组是同一谱系上的三种生态关系。

entries.definition: Either partner in a symbiosis. The relationship is symbiosis; the member is a symbiont.
entries.definitionCN: 共生关系中的任一方；关系本身是 symbiosis，成员则是 symbiont。

entries.definition: Of or relating to symbiosis. It describes the relationship, while symbiosis names it.
entries.definitionCN: 指共生的或与共生有关的；它描述这种关系，而 symbiosis 命名这种关系。

entries.definition: In a symbiotic manner. It modifies a verb, as in 'the two species live symbiotically'.
entries.definitionCN: 以共生方式地；修饰动词，如「两个物种以共生方式生活」。

entries.definition: The type of symbiosis in which both partners gain. It is a narrower and more precise term than symbiosis.
entries.definitionCN: 双方都获益的那一类共生；它比 symbiosis 更窄、更精确。

entries.definition: A relationship in which one partner benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed. It is one point on the symbiosis spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 一方获益、另一方既不受益也不受损的关系；它是共生谱系上的一个点。

entries.definition: A relationship in which one partner gains at the other's expense. In the broad definition it counts as symbiosis; in the narrow one it does not.
entries.definitionCN: 一方以另一方为代价获益的关系；按广义定义它算共生，按狭义定义则不算。

entries.definition: Working together for a shared aim. It describes behaviour and need not be a long-term biological union.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目标一起工作；它描述行为，不一定是长期的生物学结合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: syn- 'together' + bios 'life': living together, before any question of profit.
normal.cn: syn-「一起」+ bios「生命」：先讲共同生活，再谈是否获利。

normal.en: The biological term dates from 1876; the social sense is older, from the 1620s.
normal.cn: 生物学义项始于 1876 年；社会义更早，可追到十七世纪二十年代。

normal.en: The family runs symbiosis, symbioses, symbiotic, symbiotically, symbiont and endosymbiosis.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 symbiosis、symbioses、symbiotic、symbiotically、symbiont、endosymbiosis。

normal.en: The spectrum runs mutualism, commensalism, parasitism; symbiosis can name the whole range.
normal.cn: 谱系依次为互利、偏利、寄生；symbiosis 可以命名整个范围。

normal.en: The plural is symbioses, following the Greek pattern, not symbiosises.
normal.cn: 复数是 symbioses，遵循希腊语模式，而不是 symbiosises。

abstract.en: Picture two creatures sharing one room, each bringing something the other cannot make.
abstract.cn: 想象两个生物共用一间房，各自带来对方无法制造的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a factory's chimney feeding another factory's furnace.
abstract.cn: 想象一家工厂的烟囱为另一家工厂的炉子供热。

abstract.en: Picture a phone and a city changing each other until neither is the same.
abstract.cn: 想象手机与城市互相改变，直到两者都不再是原来的样子。

examples.en: Symbiosis allowed the plant to colonise dry ground.
examples.cn: 共生让这种植物得以拓殖干旱土地。

examples.en: The symbiosis of fungi and roots is older than trees.
examples.cn: 真菌与根的共生比树木本身还要古老。

examples.en: Industrial symbiosis cut both waste and cost in the park.
examples.cn: 产业共生同时降低了园区内的废物与成本。

root: 希腊 syn-「一起」（唇音前同化为 sym-）+ bios「生命」→ symbiosis「共同生活」→ 英语 symbiosis（1620s 有「社会生活」义；1876 年成为生物学词）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with cohabitation and then spread across the ecological spectrum, social partnership, industry, ecosystems and technology.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以共同居住为起点，随后铺展到生态谱系、社会伙伴、产业、生态系统与技术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two organisms side by side, arrows of exchange running both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：并排的两个生物，交换的箭头朝两个方向流动。

branches.en: COHABITATION: the root sense, long-term living together with no claim about benefit.
branches.cn: 共同居住：根义，长期共同生活，不宣称获益。

branches.en: THE SPECTRUM: mutualism, commensalism and parasitism are three points on the same axis.
branches.cn: 谱系：互利、偏利与寄生是同一轴上的三个点。

branches.en: SOCIETY: groups and institutions can live together and supply each other's lacks.
branches.cn: 社会：群体与机构可以共同生活，彼此补足所缺。

branches.en: INDUSTRY AND ECOSYSTEM: waste becomes input, and partnership keeps a system stable.
branches.cn: 产业与生态系统：废物变成投入，伙伴关系维持系统稳定。

branches.en: MUTUAL SHAPING: technology and society change each other, the furthest extension of cohabitation.
branches.cn: 相互塑造：技术与社会互相改变，这是共同居住最远的引申。

intro.en: Symbiosis is a Greek compound borrowed whole: a prefix of union, a root of life, and a Greek noun ending.
intro.cn: symbiosis 是整体借入的希腊复合词：表示「结合」的前缀、表示「生命」的词根，以及希腊名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word reached English through scientific Latin, but its parts are Greek. Latin has no native etymon for it; the Latin-looking ending -osis is a Greek transliteration.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经科学拉丁语进入英语，但其成分是希腊语；拉丁语没有它的本族词源，看似拉丁的词尾 -osis 其实是希腊语的转写。

items.exampleCN: 体表共生在珊瑚礁上很常见。

senses.title: A sign standing for an idea

senses.definitionCN: 代表某种品质或观念的事物
senses.example: The dove is a symbol of peace.
senses.exampleCN: 鸽子是和平的象征。
senses.why: The word began with a token broken in two, whose halves proved identity when rejoined.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一分为二的信物，两半合起便证明身份。

senses.title: A written or printed sign
senses.definition: a mark used to represent something in writing
senses.definitionCN: 书写中用来代表某物的记号

senses.exampleCN: 化学中水的符号是 H2O。

senses.title: A person who represents something
senses.definition: a person who stands for a cause or quality
senses.definitionCN: 代表某种事业或品质的人
senses.example: She became a symbol of courage for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这座小镇勇气的象征。
senses.why: A thing can stand for an idea, and so can a person, which extends the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 物能代表观念，人也能，这沿用了同一个逻辑。
